clue.text: Swallow a mushroom? Indeed!

indicators.note: the exclamation splits into the word in plus a noun, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a deed is an act, something done
the cep is an edible wild mushroom, the porcino

explanation.surface: Someone is dared to eat a wild mushroom and answers with an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Indeed looks like a mere exclamation of agreement; split it as 'in deed' and the mushroom sits inside the word for a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow a story or an insult is to take it on board without protest, the figurative sense of agreeing to receive it.

clue.text: More than enough to end a Cuban liberation

indicators.note: liberated letters are freed from their order and can regroup

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A demand that the Cuban struggle for freedom be brought to a close, it having gone far enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A plentiful supply exceeding need is a surplus, which is exactly a quantity greater than is required.

clue.text: Contract for a map-maker?

blocks.note: first meaning: a hire agreement, as for a boat or plane
second meaning: one who charts, a whimsical coinage, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone asks what agreement a cartographer should sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is invented: a word built from chart plus -er.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal document granting rights or hiring transport is a contract; one who draws navigational charts would literally be a charter.

clue.text: Identify styles in London and Paris, for example

blocks.note: to place someone is to recognise who they are
a style is a formal title or name

explanation.surface: Someone spots the fashions on show in two great capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: Styles looks like fashion, matching the capitals, but it means titles.
explanation.definitionFit: London and Paris are words naming locations, so both are instances of geographical names.

clue.text: This sort of parasite troubles many Francophones

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: the answer is the thing that troubles them

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variety of it, so the next word comes out in a different arrangement

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pest that plagues French speakers in particular, like an insect common across French-speaking countries.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASPIRATE is the breathy h sound; French speakers famously drop it when speaking English, so it troubles them.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetics term for the h sound breathed at the start of words, which is silent in French and so hard for native speakers to produce.

clue.text: Attacked onside, say, but disqualified

blocks.note: struck means hit or attacked
read as on side, say: in a down answer the first piece sits on the second, and the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A footballer charged in legally but was still sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: Onside suggests football, but split it: STRUCK goes on top of a side, and in cricket the field divides into on side and off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor or lawyer struck off is removed from the professional register and barred from practising.

clue.text: Indian from uncertain caste

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A person from India whose position in the caste system is unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian means a native South American here, not someone from India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the native people of the Andes whose empire Spain conquered, Indians in the old American sense.

clue.text: On the rocks — for a good reason

blocks.note: taken as written
grounds are good reasons, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: A marriage or business is failing, and justifiably so.
explanation.walkthrough: On the rocks suggests a failing relationship or whisky with ice; it is meant literally, of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel stuck on rocks or a sandbank has run onto the bottom and cannot float free.

clue.text: Go to the heart of Tyneside, for example

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letters are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters of the eight-letter word
say is used to mean for example

explanation.surface: An instruction to travel into the centre of Newcastle and its surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle in north-east England. Go here is a noun, an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go at something is attempting it, and the old noun sense of essay is a trial or attempt.

clue.text: Stand to Paddington, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: tolerate, put up with
second meaning: Paddington is the marmalade-loving creature of children's books

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take a stand towards Paddington, the London station.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington suggests the London railway station, but it is the duffel-coated character from Michael Bond's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate it; Paddington from darkest Peru is a famous fictional example of the animal.

clue.text: Ignorant lady to look out for

blocks.note: Una is the lady of the first book of Spenser's Faerie Queene, a crossword favourite
ware is an old verb meaning beware of, as in 'ware wire!'

explanation.surface: An ill-informed woman needs someone to keep an eye on her.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ignorant of a fact lacks knowledge of it, the same as not being conscious of it.

clue.text: Writes down in album

definitions.note: what is found in an album, plural

blocks.note: first meaning: puts in writing, notes for posterity
second meaning: the discs or tracks gathered in an album

explanation.surface: Someone makes notes in a scrapbook or photo album.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense and the plural noun sense share one spelling; 'in album' describes what an album holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for noting things formally and the plural of the vinyl discs collected in a music album.

clue.text: Work for the required time to achieve the right result

blocks.note: to do is to work or perform
taken as written
a trick is a sailor's set spell of duty at the helm

explanation.surface: Someone puts in the hours needed to get a job finished properly.
explanation.walkthrough: TRICK in its nautical sense is a stint at the wheel, the time a seaman is required to serve.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be effective or to accomplish what was wanted, as a remedy that works.

clue.text: Soft, fine hair, unknown to Tisiphone

blocks.note: fur is the soft fine hair of an animal's coat
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A mythological figure has never come across soft downy hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Tisiphone looks like an obscure word to define, but it is the definition: she was one of the three avenging spirits of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tisiphone, Alecto and Megaera are the three avenging goddesses of Greek mythology, each one of them an example.

clue.text: Secure means of communication for a criminal (4-

blocks.note: safe means secure
the blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: A crook needs a phone line that cannot be tapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The blower is British slang for the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who opens strongboxes with explosives is a particular kind of lawbreaker.

clue.text: Retail price controlled first in recession

indicators.note: something in recession goes back, so the word placed first runs backwards
first tells the solver that the controlled piece leads, before the word for price

blocks.note: ran a business means controlled it; first says this piece comes before the next
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: In an economic downturn, shop prices are subject to government control.
explanation.walkthrough: Retail looks like shopping, but it is the verb meaning tell over again.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail a story is to recount it in detail, an old sense of the verb meaning tell or relate.

clue.text: Common sense shown by footballer — but not initially in private

indicators.note: not initially means without its opening letter

blocks.note: a centre is a centre-forward or centre-half, a footballer by position
nous is British slang for common sense

explanation.surface: A footballer displays good sense, though not at the start, and it is kept between ourselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Not initially strips the C from CENTRE, and that piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means between ourselves, used in English for something said confidentially.

clue.text: Carried with drift at first — soon going round endlessly

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it
going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a motion that is carried is on, going ahead
anon is an old word for soon
first letter of drift

explanation.surface: Something is borne along by the current, and will soon be circling without end.
explanation.walkthrough: Endlessly looks like a deletion signal for soon, but it is the definition; ANON goes round D.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something continuing without stopping, as in talking on and on.

clue.text: Called on time and made to work

indicators.note: letters made to work are put to new use, rearranged into a fresh word

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was summoned promptly and put to work.
explanation.walkthrough: Called looks like phoned; it means named for a post.
explanation.definitionFit: To be called to an office is to be put forward or proposed for it, like a candidate chosen by a party.

clue.text: It's plain to see in English books

indicators.note: in places the word for see inside the letters for English books

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for English
vide is Latin for see, used in references
the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A remark that something is obvious from reading English literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain to see' reads as one phrase, but see is wordplay, the Latin word used in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain here is an adjective meaning obvious or clear to anyone, as in 'it's plain that he lied'.

clue.text: At home, overstretched and violent

blocks.note: in means at home
taut, strained

explanation.surface: Domestic stress boils over into violence at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent feelings or storms are extreme in force, and intense describes that same severe strength.

clue.text: Generous Carthusian shows discretion

blocks.note: free with money is generous
Dom is the title of a Carthusian or Benedictine monk

explanation.surface: A monk of a strict order turns out to be both generous and tactful.
explanation.walkthrough: Discretion looks like tact, but here it means the liberty to decide for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Discretion in the sense of choice: being left to one's own discretion is having liberty to act as one sees fit.

clue.text: Different routes from town in France

blocks.note: de is French for from; in France applies to both words
Tours is a city on the Loire

explanation.surface: A traveller heads out of a French town by other roads.
explanation.walkthrough: In France makes both pieces French: de for from, and the Loire city.
explanation.definitionFit: Diversions taken in place of the usual way are alternative paths, so the plural matches other roads.

clue.text: Announcing the end of an entertainment

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud, so the word is chosen by its sound

blocks.note: fate is one's end or doom

explanation.surface: A compere declares that the show is over.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent the answer and the word for doom sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A village or garden party with stalls and games, held outdoors as a public celebration.

clue.text: Put up a picture of a leaf

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting up means writing from bottom to top

blocks.note: an oil is an oil painting
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hangs an illustration showing a single leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaf here is a sheet of a book, not foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a single sheet of a book or manuscript, numbered on the front only.

clue.text: Italian getting into a plane in error

indicators.note: letters in error are wrongly placed and must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian passenger boards the wrong aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting into looks like the container signal, but into is fodder and the whole of 'into a plane' is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is a native of Naples, so the word is a specific sort of Italian, adjective or noun.

clue.text: Head ends up in special school — no prep!

indicators.note: ends points to the final letter of each of the following words in turn
in a down answer, up means the collected letters are written from bottom to top

blocks.note: last letter of special
last letter of school
last letter of no
last letter of prep

explanation.surface: A headmistress finishes up at a special school where pupils get no homework.
explanation.walkthrough: Head looks like a headteacher, matching the school, but it is the definition in its old sense. Prep is boarding-school slang for homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Poll is an old word for the human skull or top of the scalp, surviving in poll tax, a charge per person.

clue.text: Many a politician is wet

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
taken as written
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A dig at politicians as feeble: wet is British slang for spineless.
explanation.walkthrough: Wet in British usage also means weak and ineffectual, which drives the surface; here it means moist.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist and slightly soaked describes something damp, the literal sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Sustained a success in the distant past

blocks.note: long-lasting, sustained
taken as written
making a go of something is making a success of it

explanation.surface: An enduring triumph that happened many years back.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an adverbial meaning at a time far back in history, such as 'once upon a time'.

clue.text: Order outfit into action

blocks.note: law and order
a suit of clothes is an outfit

explanation.surface: Someone instructs a team to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: Outfit looks like a group of people and action like activity; here they are clothing and a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: An action in law is a court proceeding brought by one party against another, the same thing as a civil case.

clue.text: The highway to success — being finished first!

blocks.note: over means finished; first says it leads
a pass is success in an examination

explanation.surface: A motivational slogan: the road to winning is to be done before everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: An overpass is a road carried over another on a bridge, called a flyover in Britain.

clue.text: Wiped out in Red Sea, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters might be some other word, so rearrange them

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Recalls the Egyptian army destroyed when the waters closed over them in the Exodus.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiped out in the sense of rubbed off or deleted, as chalk from a board or text from a file.
